newsitem.title: USA: Edison ordered to build reef, wetlands.
newsitem.headline: Edison ordered to build reef, wetlands.

text.p: The California Coastal Commission decided Wednesday to require Edison International's Southern California Edison Co to restore wetlands and build an off-shore reef to compensate for environmental harm caused by the San Onofre nuclear power plant near San Clemente.

Edison has 60 days to choose whether to conduct the work itself or to establish a $117.65 million trust fund for the commission to implement the projects, said a spokeswoman for the state commission said Thursday.
The company can also choose to bring legal action against the commission's decision, she noted.
A spokesman for Edison said the company was not clear on the details of the trust fund.
Edison had sought to revise a 1991 agreement to construct a 300-acre artificial kelp reef off the coast of San Clemente which it said was not justified by scientific evidence.

The company offered instead to build a smaller, 17-acre reef in addition to projects, like fish hatcheries, it had already undertaken to make up for the environmental impact of ocean water intake at the nuclear plant.

The staff of the commission proposed a compromise plan for a 122-acre reef to be funded by a trust fund, but the commission voted Wednesday for funding of a 150-acre reef and restoration of 150 acres of wetlands.
Edison owns 75 percent of the San Onofre project, which consists of a 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit and a 1,080 MW unit.
Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co holds a 20 percent stake in the plant and two municipal utilities share the remaining five percent.
